name: cross-boundary-field-thread
body:
## Thread `dispatch_attempt` through the run-status surface

The runner records a per-stage `dispatch_attempt` counter, but nothing downstream can read it. Thread it end to end so an operator can see how many times a stage was dispatched without reading the trace bundle.

### Boundaries it has to cross

- `backend/internal/db` — the column already exists on `stages`; the sqlc row struct does not select it.
- `backend/internal/run` — the domain `Stage` struct has no field for it.
- `backend/internal/server` — `stageResponse` / `toStageResponse` in `reads.go` must carry it.
- `docs/api/v0.openapi.yaml` and `docs/api/v0.md` — the response schema is source of truth.

### Done means

1. `GET /v0/runs/{id}/stages/{id}` returns `dispatch_attempt` as an integer.
2. A value written by the runner survives the whole round trip, asserted by ONE integration test that crosses every boundary above — not four per-layer unit tests that pass while the seam is broken.
3. The OpenAPI document and its human companion both describe the field.
expectation_note: A good plan scopes EVERY boundary named above (db row, domain struct, server response, both API docs) and plans the single cross-boundary integration test done-means item 2 demands, rather than per-layer units. Dropping a boundary or substituting per-layer tests is the requirement-coverage failure this fixture is chosen to detect.
